reason: Driven and reproduced exactly, on the real first-run path (owner-empty, type 3 October 2026, Set the day, Add a moment). render-b.js:1474 writes F.project.primaryDate = { label: "The day", date: started } and no control in the artifact ever writes that field again - the full data-act inventory is add/copy/delete/done/owner/preview/publish/retry/setday, and none of them names the day. The constant is then spent as a fact in four render sites: the horizon subtitle (render-b.js:116) prints "AISLING & TOM / 79 days / Saturday 3 October 2026 / The day", carried unchanged into Preview and into print, which renders the same horizon; the stepper ceiling (render-b.js:651) and the typed-date refusal (render-b.js:922) both print "This is as far as it goes. The day is the last day.", a tautology no one wrote; and the unfurl card (render-b.js:1605) titles the thing that lands in the couple's message "The day, Saturday 3 October 2026". The graded frames all show the fixture's "Wedding day" (fixture.js:95), so every frame the panel scored displays a value no project started in this product can produce - the fixture flattering the artifact on the one asset that leaves it. Not already handled: nothing sets the label, and the day-is-set screen asks nothing further. Not a gate restatement: interaction-check only asserts /as far as it goes/ matches and never inspects the label; the .b-sub assertion at line 2552 is the loading state's own unrelated .b-sub (render-b.js:1821), so guarding the horizon's does not touch it. SCOPE: this is a design change, not a schema change. primaryDate.label already exists in the record and is already read in four places; the fix collects a value for a field the model has, invents no field, and needs no migration. The renderer's own comment at render-b.js:113 draws exactly this line - inventing a venue field would be the data-model change, which is why the subtitle was pointed at label in the first place. Where the finding overreaches is fix (c). Interpolating F.fmt.longYear into the ceiling sentence prints "Saturday 3 October 2026" directly beneath .b-stepRead, which at the ceiling already reads "Saturday 3 October 2026 - in 79 days", with #b-edit-date showing "3 Oct 2026" above it: the same date three times inside one 90px block, and the same duplication the panel already refuted twice for the editor's reserved band. Fix (a) as written also inserts a third screen between the date and the plan, which is a real cost on the flow round 8 just tightened. The defect is real and the cure is cheap; the proposed cure needs the sharpening below.
sharpenedFix: Three edits, none touching the schema. (1) Stop writing a placeholder as data: in states["owner-empty"] set { label: "", date: started } (render-b.js:1474) - a string the product invented must never be read back as a fact about the record. (2) Guard the two consumers: in horizon() render .b-sub only when label is non-empty (.b-sub is margin:0 and .b-todayRule carries its own --gap-block top margin, so removal is spacing-safe, and print inherits the same guard); in card() build .b-unfurlTitle as the nowrap date alone when label is empty, dropping the leading text node and its comma, so the card reads "Saturday 3 October 2026" rather than "The day, ...". (3) Take the label out of the ceiling sentence entirely rather than swapping the date in: in setAway() and commitDate() use "This is as far as it goes. Nothing can sit after the day itself." That is true on every project including the fixture, keeps the /as far as it goes/ the gate asserts, matches the language the gate already uses for the rule, and does not print the long date a second time under .b-stepRead. Then, to actually let a plan be named, do NOT add a screen: put one optional field on the day-is-set screen that already exists - label "The day is", placeholder "Wedding day", sitting above the existing "Add a moment" primary, writing to primaryDate.label on blur or on the same press. Measured room exists (.b-empty is 476px of 844 at 390x844; ~70px more at 1440 costs a little scroll on a screen already at 993px). The flow keeps its two steps, "it is the only thing needed to start" stays literally true, and the line that carries the feeling of the product stops shipping as a placeholder.
